name: Izere (Retired)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Retired bookkeeping code [fiz]; sole Glottolog ref is the ISO 639-3 change request 2007-147; see izer1241 for the living language.

new_statements.quote: Izere has 29 consonant phonemes, 7 vowel phonemes and 3 level tones. [...] There are five tones in Izere, three level and two contour tones (LM & HL). Contour tones occur in loanwords, words with potentially onomatopoeic names such as those of birds and where a tonally dissimilar VV sequence has been shortened. As such these synchronic occurrences are probably transitional and Izere can be regarded as having an underlying three-height system.
new_statements.citation: Blench, Roger & Bitrus Kaze. 2019. A dictionary of the Izere language of Fobur (2019 edition). Jos/Cambridge: electronic ms. (rogerblench.info, via Wayback). Front matter, section 4.1 'Izere phonology'.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Izere is described as a register-tone language with three level tones (H, M, L) plus marginal LM and HL contours; word stress or accent is not mentioned in any opened description, so no stress rule can be stated.
new_statements.exceptions: Contour tones arise only in loanwords, onomatopoeic (bird) names and shortened VV sequences.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical (citation-form) tone as marked in the dictionary; nothing said about phrase-level prominence. The description is of the Fobur (Ibor) variety of Izere, i.e. izer1241 [izr], not of the retired code.
new_statements.identity_note: izer1243 is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry for the retired ISO 639-3 code [fiz] 'Izere', split by change request 2007-147 (effective 2008-01-14) into [izr] Izere = izer1241 and [gne] Ganang = gana1270. Its only Glottolog reference is the change-request form, which contains no linguistic description. All descriptive material (Blench & Kaze 2019 dictionary front matter, Blench 2000, Blench n.d., Erin 2022; unopened Lukas & Willms 1961 etc.) belongs to izer1241 (Fobur/Ibor Izere); Ganang gana1270 has no descriptive sources at all. Per the fleet census-counting law, a retired code confers no identity, so any catalog entry built from the quoted statement should be filed under izer1241, not izer1243.

sources.note: No mention of stress/accent anywhere (grep for stress|accent|prominen|suprasegment finds only the tone-diacritic table). States 29 consonants, 7 vowels, three level tones plus two contour tones (LM, HL) that are 'probably transitional'; underlying three-height tone system; dictionary fully tone-marked.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. Research on the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Uebersee 93: 1-49. doi:10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.209
sources.note: Survey only. Izere cluster passage (p.20): 'The Izere language spoken in Fobur has been the subject of several unpublished analyses and has an orthography and a translation of the New Testament. It is divided into seven dialects... A draft dictionary and sketches of several aspects of the grammar have been published on the internet (Blench n.d.: Izere page).' No stress or phonology statement for Izere; reference list has Lukas & Willms 1961, Gerhardt 1984, Wolff & Meyer-Bahlburg 1979.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-147: split [fiz] Izere into [izr] Izere and [gne] Ganang (adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International, 8 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone; only rationale for the split: 'The phonology and noun-class system of Ganang have taken on features of Berom and it is, for all practical purposes, unintelligible to mainstream Izere-speakers' (p.3). Sole source cited is Blench's 2001 Nigeria minority-languages list.
